He was born on 18 May 1854 in the village of Kishoreganj, in the present-day Bangladesh. He was influenced by the works of the great Bengali poet, Michael Madhusudan Dutt, and began writing poetry at a young age. He is best known for his works in the genre of 'Mohabbat Kabya' (love poems) and 'Natak' (plays).

Chandrakishore Pande was a prominent leader in the Indian Independence Movement. He was born in the year 1873 in the village of Kandi, in the present-day Madhya Pradesh, India. He was educated in Lahore and later joined the Indian National Congress. He was arrested in 1916 for his involvement in the Non-Cooperation Movement and was imprisoned until 1921. After his release, he continued his activism and was arrested again in 1932 for participating in the Civil Disobedience Movement. He was released in 1934 and remained active in the Indian National Congress until his death in 1947.
